newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 20.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:
* The U.S. trade deficit widened in December, bringing the year's figure to $114.2 billion, the largest gap since 1988.

* There's a reason the Japanese yen comes across as the weakling of the currency markets these days: Japan, with its struggling economy, frail stock market and cheap funds, has become a place to borrow, not invest. -- Market Place.
* Time Warner said it will sell its interest in American Lawyer Media and Counsel Connect, but keep its interest in Court TV.

* Europe's freight rail systems are being modernized with help from American railroad companies including Wisconsin Central Transportation and CSX Corp as the continent prepares for economic unification.
* Consumer prices rose one-tenth of one percent in January, below the consensus forecast of three-tenths of one percent.

* General Motors is considering selling up to 20 percent of its automotive and electronics auto parts units after it combines the units - Delco Electronics and Delphi Automotive Systems - into the world's biggest automotive supplier.

* AFL-CIO leaders voted against extending the North American Free Trade Agreement to other countries unless the pact includes labor and environmental protections that were rejected by the Clinton Administration.
* Authorities say telephone and Internet marketers are joining with telecommunications companies in emerging nations to cheat unwary consumers around the world.
* Advertising agencies True North Communications of Chicago and Publicis of Paris agreed to end their dispute over the dissolution of a global business alliance.
* Goldman Sachs continued the broadening of its top management by naming two new vice chairmen.
* The Fed approved rules making it easier for banks to offer new products and buy other financial institutions.
* Compaq Computer plans to announce that it is entering the market for personal computers priced less than $1,000.
* WMX agreed to sell its 19 percent interest in ServiceMaster back to ServiceMaster.
* The Venezuelan government said it would not spend any more money on its ailing state airline, Viasa.
* The Detroit Free Press and The Detroit News told workers who had been on strike that former strikers will only get their jobs back as jobs become available.
* Stock prices dropped in late-afternoon trading, and the yield on the 30-year Treasury bond rose to 6.57 percent.
